fp8_gemm.tile_rule: M=128*MmaSM,N=128,K=TileK; two-SM means M256/N128, not N256.
fp8_gemm.scale_rule: ScaleMajorK=true means both A/B FP32 scales K-major. false means both MN-major. Public checkpoint weight scales remain row-major; stateless packing is in fp8.py for the selected large MN case.
fp8_gemm.default_public_argument: groupwise.gemm(...,scale_major_k=True); production fp8._project_quantized explicitly passes not mn.
fp8_gemm.production_selection: Owned GEMM for M>32. mma_sm2 when physical M>=4096 and N>=32768. MN only for logical M>=32144 and exact weight(34816,5120); otherwise K-major. Small<=32 uses separate FlashInfer TRT backend.
fp8_gemm.workspace: 16B per stream, bounded4 streams/device. get_workspace_size(arguments) checked against allocation before initialize/run; larger future requirements fail closed.
fp8_gemm.stream_pdl: gemm.initialize(arguments,workspace_ptr,caller_stream), then gemm.run(caller_stream,nullptr,pdl). Keep inherited CUTLASS PDL provider contract; no source synchronization change.
fp8_gemm.swizzle: full two-SM gate/up16; else M>=2048 and N>=32768 ->8; else full QKVZ16; else full down8; otherwise0.
fp8_gemm.excluded_operation: BF16 vocabulary logits_gemm uses FlashInfer mm_bf16(cute-dsl) or F.linear, never owned FP8.

paired_groupwise_accum.protocol: Two independent N-tile TMEM loads into separate registers precede one wait. Preserve each output K-group ordering, FP32 scale multiply/FMA, final wait before pipeline release and final BF16 RNE conversion.

findings.title: contiguous_bf16_rows_kernel fires PDL trigger after the copy loop — no proven downstream PDL overlap with current consumer
findings.reachable_trigger: GDN prefill when _contiguous_values matches the owned CUDA fast guard for packed BF16 V; other layouts use already-contiguous data or PyTorch contiguous().

evidence.description: The copy waits at entry and triggers after its loop. GDN._contiguous_values feeds chunk_gated_delta_rule, not FA2. The pinned GDN API has no PDL parameter and its SM100 CuTe launch supplies no explicit PDL enable flag. Earlier triggering alone has no demonstrated downstream overlap benefit. This is a placement fact and future integration question, not a current defect.

findings.original_finding_error: Original F01 stated the consumer was 'paged FA2' and asserted that moving the trigger earlier would allow FA2 prolog overlap. Both claims are false. Consumer is FlashInfer chunk_gated_delta_rule, which uses no PDL.
findings.recommended_fix: No production change warranted given the current consumer. If a future GDN prefill consumer gains PDL support, revisit trigger placement at that time.
findings.validation: Any future PDL-capable consumer integration would require a Nsight Systems timeline comparison showing kernel prolog overlap before claiming benefit.
findings.measured_scope: Source inspection of placement/caller chain. No new latency comparison or PDL gain claimed.

findings.title: FP8 medium-projection high long-scoreboard stall rate — measured observation, root cause not proven
findings.source_lines: CutlassGroupwiseScaledGEMMSM100 medium projection dispatch; PairedGroupwiseAccum mainloop

evidence.type: existing measured Nsight counters plus source inspection
evidence.description: This a6b9bd2 profile matches current groupwise source/header bytes and loaded module. longSB35.26%, shortSB13.01%, issue_active46.29%, eligible0.65 average eligible warps per active scheduler cycle (raw unit warp), SM throughput62.91%, DRAM throughput13.51%, registers168, dynamic SMEM201216B, active-warps occupancy11.83%. Long-scoreboard is not an exclusive wall-time fraction or proof of TMEM latency. This record has no PC/SASS attribution of the dominant cause.

original_finding_errors: eligible0.65 was described as0.65%; raw unit is warp and the metric is per active scheduler cycle.
Long-scoreboard was asserted to establish TMEM latency and a unique SMEM remedy.
Original values lacked an explicit record binding. They are now verified current-source facts, not mislabelled C9 counters.
findings.recommended_fix: Retain the measured stall observation. If future work targets this shape, PC/SASS attribution is needed to identify the dominant stall source before attempting stage reduction or accumulator changes. The packed FP32 candidate (F04) provides a complementary direction with existing measurements.
findings.validation: Any tuning selection needs source-bound numerical and whole-operation timing checks; PC/SASS attribution can test the hypothesized pipeline cause before selecting an intervention.
findings.measured_scope: Current-source profile of M624/N34816/K5120 only. No all-shape or wall-time inference. The earlier portable C10 record with 33.95% and 0.56 warp is a separate valid measurement, not conflicting evidence.

findings.title: Packed FP32 candidate:18 complete-operation comparisons,10 speed passes/8 failures;7 common GEMM geometries cover9 passing operations

evidence.description: All 18 shapes bitwise correct. Speed results from packed_candidate_rows: passing shapes (speed_passed=true) are M624N34816K5120 normalized-gateup, M624N16384K5120 qkvz, M624N5120K17408 silu-down, M624N5120K6144 gated-out, M1248N5120K17408 silu-down, M1248N5120K6144 out, M1248N5120K6144 gated-out, M2496N5120K17408 silu-down, M2496N5120K6144 out, M2496N5120K6144 gated-out (10 total). Failing shapes (speed_passed=false): M624N14336K5120 qkv, M624N5120K6144 out, M1248N34816K5120 normalized-gateup, M1248N16384K5120 qkvz, M1248N14336K5120 qkv, M2496N34816K5120 normalized-gateup, M2496N16384K5120 qkvz, M2496N14336K5120 qkv (8 total). Failing geometries are not unknown; the JSON enumerates them. Seven common geometries covering nine complete operations share the passing config.

findings.original_finding_error: Original F04 stated 'failing shapes not yet identified'; the external JSON fully enumerates them.
findings.recommended_fix: No production adoption is established. Geometry dispatch must cover all operations sharing the same GEMM: M624/N5120/K6144 cannot be selected from gated-out alone because plain out failed. Seven common geometries cover nine consistently passing operations, not all ten individual passes. Adoption requires independent production full-operation/framework validation.
findings.validation: Full-operation framework validation required before any production dispatch change.
findings.measured_scope: External diagnostic:18 complete-operation comparisons, all bitwise equal;10 positive paired speed gates/8 failures. Rows624/1248/2496. The7 common geometries cover9 operations because out and gated-out share each M/N/K. These medium cases do not validate two-SM or large MN dispatch.

findings.title: DSpark attention draft block is fully bidirectional — no causal masking, matches reference

evidence.description: kernels.cu line 2315: 'const int context = contexts[seq], last = context + 7;' — last is invariant across all query rows. Line 2380: 'int length = row < end ? last : 0;' — length=last=context+7 for all valid rows (row<end). Score predicate: row<end && base+col<length. There is no col<=row cutoff; every valid draft row can attend every position in [context, context+7). ir/dspark.py line 104: 'out = torch.einsum("qhrk,khd->qhrd", scores.softmax(-1), value)' — reference also applies no causal mask. tests/test_dspark_kernel_reference.py line 53 test explicitly verifies all queries see all noise rows.
evidence.source_line_2315: const int context = contexts[seq], last = context + 7;

findings.original_finding_error: Original F07 claimed the kernel applies causal masking within the 7-row draft block while the reference does not. Both kernel and reference are fully bidirectional for valid rows; no divergence exists. Existing test at tests/test_dspark_kernel_reference.py line 53 explicitly covers this.
findings.validation: Source inspection and existing test coverage confirm correctness.

Line 128: 'tensor.copy_(dynamic[name])' — copy only after all shape checks pass. tests/test_prefill_graph.py line 13: 'def test_failure_preserves_storage_then_valid_replay_succeeds(failure):' — existing test covers failed planner followed by valid replay. findings.title: Multi-stream side-stream error attribution — eager debug mode already provides per-operation attribution
findings.reachable_trigger: Any GPU error on the side stream during multi_stream execution.

evidence.description: gdn_prepare.py line 155: 'origin.wait_stream(side)' — wait_stream queues an event dependency and returns immediately on the CPU; async errors are not guaranteed to surface at this join point. kernels.cu line 93: 'void finish_cuda_launch(cudaStream_t stream, const char *operation)' with line 100: '<< operation << " CUDA execution error observed after launch: "' — OH_MY_VLLM_CUDA_DEBUG_SYNC eager mode already checks and synchronizes each owned operation individually with an operation label. The original recommendation to call torch.cuda.check_error() was incorrect: check_error(res:int) checks a supplied runtime return code, not a stream; calling it without an argument is not valid. Altering the default path to synchronize would eliminate overlap.
evidence.source_line_100: << operation << " CUDA execution error observed after launch: "

findings.original_finding_error: Original F10 recommended 'torch.cuda.check_error()' for stream error attribution — check_error() takes an int return code, not a stream, so the recommendation was technically wrong. The existing OH_MY_VLLM_CUDA_DEBUG_SYNC mode already provides per-operation attribution without altering the default overlap path.
findings.recommended_fix: No default-path change needed. Existing eager debug mode (OH_MY_VLLM_CUDA_DEBUG_SYNC) is the correct tool for debugging side-stream errors.
findings.validation: Source inspection confirms existing debug infrastructure.

findings.title: attention_partial_kernel double-buffering already present for batch=4 ungrouped — original blanket claim was false
findings.category: performance — already implemented for the relevant dispatch

findings.reachable_trigger: Ungrouped decode with q.size(0)==4 already uses Buffers=2 (next-tile prefetch).

evidence.description: kernels.cu line 1782: 'if constexpr (Buffers == 2) {' — next-tile cp.async prefetch via stage_kv is present and active for Buffers=2. Line 1949: '// Only four ungrouped queries benefit from double buffering on B200.' Line 1969: 'ATTENTION(true, false, 2);' dispatches Buffers=2 for ungrouped q.size(0)==4. Grouped decode (h==24&&hk==4) and other ungrouped batch sizes use Buffers=1 by deliberate dispatch decision. The short-prefix diagnostic 15 FA calls (6.0ms) are FlashInfer prefill calls, not measurements of this owned decode kernel.
evidence.source_line_1949: // Only four ungrouped queries benefit from double buffering on B200.

findings.original_finding_error: Original F11 claimed 'no double-buffered prefetch for the next KV tile.' Buffers=2 with stage_kv prefetch already exists and is dispatched for the relevant batch size. The Buffers=1 dispatch for grouped and other paths is a deliberate measured decision (line 1949), not an omission.
findings.recommended_fix: No change needed. If grouped or other batch sizes need double buffering, measure first — the dispatch comment at line 1949 indicates the B200 benefit applies specifically to four ungrouped queries.

findings.measured_scope: N/A — correctness of dispatch confirmed. Performance of the owned decode kernel at large contexts not separately profiled.

findings.title: mma_sm=2 MN-major production path correct — experimental two-SM failure isolated to rejected code

findings.reachable_trigger: MN only for full gate/up logical M>=32144,N34816,K5120, explicitly selected by fp8._project_quantized. Public groupwise.gemm defaults scale_major_k=True; two-SM4096..32143 gate/up remains K-major.

evidence.description: ScaleMajorK=true maps both scales K-major;false maps both MN-major. FFI restricts MN to the large full two-SM gate/up shape. Standard K-major remains a valid production branch. The medium18 diagnostic rows624/1248/2496 are all below the production two-SM threshold4096, so they do not validate MN/two-SM. Also: original report described SM=2 tiles as N256; actual tile is M256/N128 (MmaTileShape_MNK = Shape<MmaSM*128, 128, TileK>).
findings.recommended_fix: No production change. Use dedicated large MN/formal/replay evidence for that branch; medium18 supplies no such acceptance.
findings.validation: Dispatch/layout source facts verified. Existing tests/test_fp8_mn_replay.py and large formal cases have separate scope; this review reruns none and claims no new acceptance.
findings.measured_scope: Medium18 supports its own complete-operation results only. This review establishes no new large-M numerical/performance result.

BF16 finite path: rcp.approx.ftz.f32 + one quotient-refinement step using two nested __fmaf_rn operations (kernels.cu lines 211, 224). FP16/FP32/nonfinite: exact __fdiv_rn. All production dtypes correctly covered.
